https://www.naturalnews.com/2026-08-08-z.text: Zelensky's Washington Visit Produces No New Commitments Ukrainian President Vladimir Zelensky met with U.S. President Donald Trump in Washington last week, according to a report published by RT. The meeting lasted less than an hour and produced no new military aid packages or shift in Trump's public position, the report said. Zelensky had sought an immediate meeting with Trump to finalize a peace deal, fearing dwindling Western support amid battlefield losses and corruption scandals [1]. The only concrete outcome of the visit was an agreement for Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff to travel to Kyiv, the report stated. The meeting came after Trump had rejected Zelensky's urgent request for long-range Tomahawk cruise missiles in October 2025, arguing that such weapons would undermine the prospects for a negotiated settlement [2]. Trump had also ordered an immediate halt to U.S. military aid and intelligence sharing earlier in 2025, with the Pentagon confirming that Ukraine-bound planes were turned around midflight [3]. The report said the latest encounter avoided a repeat of the February 2025 Oval Office confrontation, but that avoiding disaster did not amount to achieving success. Careful PR Effort Preceded Meeting The visit was preceded by a carefully orchestrated public relations campaign, according to the report. Much of the Western mainstream media greeted Zelensky with glowing coverage, and several MAGA-aligned bloggers who had previously been hostile to Kyiv adopted a friendlier tone. Zelensky also attempted to strengthen his position by raising tensions with Iran, reportedly bringing intelligence on U.S. adversaries to the White House, the report stated. Reports from March 2026 indicated that the Kremlin had proposed an intelligence swap involving Iran to halt U.S. aid to Ukraine, a sign of the degree to which Iran-related leverage was in play [4]. Zelensky's team reportedly believed that presenting Trump with carefully selected information would change his policy, but the analysis concluded this was a fundamental misreading. The report noted that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu succeeded in pushing Trump to confront Iran because that aligned with Trump's existing instincts, while Ukraine did not share that alignment. The report said the strategic assumption that Trump could be convinced through facts alone was not supported by his record. Outcomes Limited to Agreement on Kyiv Visit Trump described the meeting as having gone "very well," a phrase he routinely applies to almost every high-level conversation, according to the report. No new military aid packages were announced, there was no escalation of pressure on Moscow, and no endorsement of Zelensky followed. The report said the funeral of Sen. Lindsey Graham appeared to occupy more of Trump's attention than the war in Ukraine on the day of the meeting. The only concrete result was an agreement for Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff to visit Kyiv, which the report described as a modest outcome for a trip presented as strategically important. Ukraine had previously secured a resumption of U.S. intelligence sharing and military aid after accepting a 30-day ceasefire proposal in March 2025 [5], but that support has not expanded into a deeper commitment. Trump's announcement in October 2025 of plans to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin in Budapest further indicated a shift away from Kyiv's preferred posture [6]. Report Attributes Failure to Misreading Trump The report attributed Zelensky's failure to an incorrect assumption that Trump could be manipulated by presenting him with selective information. Trump has been politically consistent on key issues for decades, having criticized U.S. allies in 1987 for relying excessively on American military protection and having advocated a confrontational policy toward Iran, the report said. Zelensky had previously downplayed Trump's public statements about forcing a negotiated settlement, telling CNN's "Fareed Zakaria GPS" that it was important to understand election messages [7]. The report said Trump's view of Ukraine has long been tied to domestic U.S. politics, with modern Ukraine associated in his mind with Barack Obama and Joe Biden. The conflict has been described as a predictable consequence of NATO expansion, with former CIA Director William Burns warning in 2008 that drawing Ukraine into NATO would lead to civil war and Russian intervention [8]. The report concluded that a well-managed public relations campaign could not erase perceptions formed years before Zelensky's diplomacy began. U.S. Constraints Cited as Obstacles The report cited practical obstacles to Ukraine's requests, noting that U.S. weapons stockpiles have been depleted by multiple conflicts and that expanding production of systems like Patriot missiles will take years. The United States carries almost $40 trillion in national debt, the report said, increasing political resistance to further large-scale commitments. Ukraine had ratified a minerals deal granting Washington 50% of revenues from critical minerals and infrastructure projects [9], but financial and material constraints remained. American public support for Ukraine has declined over the course of the war. An AP-NORC poll found support at 48 percent, a 12 percent drop from the 60 percent approval recorded in May of the previous year [10]. The United States has contributed over $73 billion in aid, according to the Kiel Institute for the World Economy [11], while Kyiv has faced mounting pressure, including 60,000 desertion cases launched in 2024 and significant territorial losses [12]. Trump imposed sanctions on Russian oil companies Rosneft and Lukoil in October 2025, a move that Russian analysts said "hit Moscow â but missed the point" [13]. The report concluded that the battle Zelensky traveled to Washington to win had been lost before his plane landed. The combination of depleted U.S. stockpiles, a $40 trillion national debt, declining public support, and Trump's consistent foreign policy instincts meant the outcomes Zelensky sought were never likely to materialize, the analysis said. https://www.politico.eu/article/europes-.text: Europe’s biggest political family is already preparing its 2029 election strategy to win back voters from the far right — even as its own members split over whether to work with those parties and how far to follow them on policy. The center-right European People’s Party chair, Manfred Weber, internally launched a “Win2029” task force two weeks ago. The main goal of the group will be to develop an attractive enough policy platform to take on the far right at the polls in three years’ time. But interviews and internal meeting records reveal deepening disagreements over cooperation with far-right groups and how closely to align with them on migration, climate and social issues. Advertisement “The main polarization across the continent in many national elections, and certainly in the European election 2029 … will be the anti-European populists against the EPP parties,” said EPP vice-chair and Romanian prime minister nominee Siegfried Mureșan. Anything beyond the “battle” between EPP and the far right “will be of secondary importance,” echoed the conservative group’s spokesperson Pedro López de Pablo. “Because they are not in government, they can promise the earth. Faced with that kind of rhetoric, we need to think of which alternatives we can offer to the people.” Siegfried Mureșan participates in a meeting in Brussels on June 26, 2025. | Martin Bertrand/Hans Lucas/AFP via Getty Images With the European Parliament not yet halfway through its current term, the task force marks an unusually early start to the EPP’s 2029 election preparations — and underscores the urgency party leaders feel as far-right parties gain ground across the bloc. Led by Spanish MEP Esteban González Pons, the task force will help draft the party’s final electoral program. Talks are due to start at an October retreat in Sicily and continue through next spring’s EPP congress in Rome. EPP lawmakers are already wrestling with the choice ahead. “This is the political history, the historical dilemma EPP needs to decide — it needs to be clear and it needs be truthful for the voters, are we center right or are we another right-wing party? ” said Finnish EPP lawmaker Sirpa Pietikäinen. Advertisement To deal or not to deal The divisions reflect different political realities across the party. In some countries, governing with the far right has become a political reality; in others, those parties remain the EPP’s main rivals and cooperation is a red line. Poles and Romanians oppose any alignment with the far right, while conservatives in Spain, Sweden, Finland, Denmark and the Netherlands have governed with them. German lawmakers are divided, as some in Berlin start questioning the firewall against Alternative for Germany (AfD) given its recent electoral successes. Yet most German EPP members in Brussels remain opposed. “There has always been that discussion within the party: Whether we should put content first, or the centrist platform first,” said Finnish EPP delegation chief Mika Aaltola. Mika Aaltola sits in the European Parliament in Brussels on July 16, 2025. | Martin Bertrand/Hans Lucas/AFP via Getty Images Meeting notes from the past six months show the EPP attempting to maintain its firewall in the Parliament, with lawmakers repeatedly instructed to reject the far-right Patriots’ initiatives while backing similar proposals from the right-wing European Conservatives and Reformists, home to Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni. The EPP considers ECR an acceptable partner. To make an example of one of its lawmakers and quell criticism, the group went as far as to expel Slovenian MEP Branko Grims after he appeared at an event organized by the AfD. Yet the EPP cannot escape the temptation to go with far-right groups on sensitive issues where agreement with the Socialists and Democrats is harder to reach. Advertisement That happened recently on the EU’s long-term budget file, when a right-wing majority voted to strip green and gender criteria from spending oversight. EPP leaders had vowed to stick with the center but could not keep lawmakers in line, exposing a divide now spilling into day-to-day legislative battles. At its last plenary, the EPP group discussed how to pass a resolution on the migration crisis in Ceuta, the Spanish territory, after negotiations with the Socialists and Democrats collapsed. Two sets of internal notes seen by POLITICO show the strategy was to make the Patriots feel “included” by deliberately backing one of their amendments. A temporary migrant camp is set up at El Trampolín beach in Ceuta, Spain, where more than 2,000 migrants are estimated to be living, according to the latest figures on Sept. 24, 2026. | Manu Brabo/Getty Images The idea came from the Spanish delegation, which wanted a political win in Madrid. EPP leaders backed the plan, urging lawmakers to support the text whether or not the Patriots’ amendments passed. Migration tensions The EPP’s bigger challenge may be not whether to work with the far right, but whether to fight it on its issues or shift the political agenda onto its own terrain — and, in doing so, whether to move right to win back voters or stand their ground in the center. At the congress following the 2024 EU election, Weber made clear that he wanted to reshape the party’s “narrative” to regain support from voters tempted by far-right populists. That meant tougher migration policies, more deportations and rolling back green rules — positions that have only hardened since. Even as the EU’s Migration Pact introduced faster asylum and border procedures in June, and negotiators agreed on bloc-wide rules to speed up deportations, the EPP pushed for tougher measures. Advertisement At its Vienna political assembly that month, it called for more investment in Frontex, the EU’s coast guard agency, and easier returns at the bloc’s external border. Delegates also agreed to replace “irregular migration” with “illegal migration” throughout the text, adopting language more commonly associated with the far right, according to the confidential minutes. That migration strategy is raising eyebrows within the party. During a heated debate on political Islam in Europe in the same assembly, EPP Vice President and former Commissioner Mairead McGuinness warned colleagues “against conflating religious faith with political extremism,” calling for “a clear commitment to freedom of religion,” the minutes read. A French member of Frontex works at the cross-Channel terminal in Calais, France on July 25, 2024. | Bernard Barron/AFP via Getty Images German EPP lawmaker Dennis Radtke, who leads the party’s wing in charge of relations with trade unions, told POLITICO the party should avoid blaming the far right’s rise on migration alone. “Of course we have to ensure secure borders, no doubt about that, but to link the success of the extreme right in Europe only with the question of migration … I have doubts that this is the case,” he said. “The asylum seeker numbers are going down; the extreme right is still going up because a lot of social problems are not solved or even touched.” Culture wars As competitiveness and deregulation dominate the EPP’s response to Europe’s economic woes, some fear social and workers’ rights are being sidelined. Advertisement In February, the party’s workers’, seniors’ and women’s wings pushed a resolution calling for stronger social protections, skills and youth employment support. Austrian, Finnish, German and Swedish delegates came out against it, accusing it of being “poorly framed”, as “its focus on social justice sends the wrong signal given EPP priorities on competitiveness and productivity,” according to meeting minutes. Other lawmakers pushed back, arguing the party could not abandon the social dimension. The leadership postponed the vote, and the resolution quietly disappeared from the next meeting’s agenda. “It has not become easier,” said Radtke of trying to strengthen the EPP’s social focus. “If we are not willing to deliver on workers’ rights, on social issues, then we cannot claim to be Europe’s last people’s party.” Mairead McGuinness speaks during a press conference at the EU headquarters in Brussels on June 27, 2023. | Kenzo Tribouillard/AFP via Getty Images The far right’s culture wars are also reverberating inside the EPP, where longstanding tensions over feminism, gender and reproductive rights are shifting in favor of the conservative camp. In Parliament, the EPP has traditionally backed strong sexual and reproductive rights while allowing national delegations a free vote on abortion, said veteran gender equality MEP Pietikäinen. Now, as some delegations harden their positions, consensus is eroding and more issues — including gender budgeting, which examines how public spending affects women and men — are left to free votes. “Now it has been more difficult,” she said. A report on gender inequalities in health descended into pandemonium at an EPP group meeting last plenary, as Irish, Polish and Luxembourgish lawmakers urged colleagues to back it, while Spaniards called it “crazy” and Croatians denounced its “gender ideology” as “radical” and “extreme.” Advertisement The party’s vow to simplify EU legislation has also opened rifts, as lawmakers disagree on how far to scrap green laws. Its factions are divided over how far to weaken the combustion-engine phaseout, and how much to soften industry’s carbon emission restrictions under the Emissions Trading System, which puts a price on industrial emissions. The disputes expose the EPP’s central dilemma ahead of 2029: whether to harden its positions to win back voters from the far right or hold the center — a choice that risks deepening divisions among its national parties. Gabriel Gavin contributed reporting.

Photograph: John Amis/AP Mississippi Friends of Nolan Wells sue NFL Hall of Famer Terrell Owens for defamation Owens sued over September Instagram post that suggested trio tampered with evidence in death of Mississippi teen Uwa Ede-Osifo Tue 6 Oct 2026 22.04 EDT Last modified on Tue 6 Oct 2026 22.05 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Three friends of Nolan Wells , a Mississippi teen who died after a July boating trip, have sued NFL Hall of Famer Terrell Owens for defamation. On 26 September, Owens shared an Instagram video that suggested Wells’s friends Warren Hudson, Jax Pitalo and Morgan Seymour had deleted evidence from Wells’s phone after his death, which the three men denied in their lawsuit. “Arrest them immediately!! Like yesterday,” Owens captioned the post. In a Monday complaint filed in a Mississippi district court, the fathers of the three young men, who are also named in the complaint as plaintiffs because they are deemed minors under state law, accuse Owens of harming their reputation and endangering their physical safety with the post. “Due to the conduct of Owens and many other less-famous individuals, these completely innocent young men have been subjected to thousands of death threats, face-to-face harassment, and daily fear and ridicule from complete strangers. They’ve even been refused service at public establishments. Their lives, and the lives of their family members, will never be the same,” the complaint alleges. Owens could not be immediately reached for comment. The friends’ counsel also indicated they intend to take legal action against other public figures who have been vocal about Wells’s death including Al Sharpton and The View’s Sunny Hostin. On 4 July, Wells and his friends sailed for a Mississippi island. He was last seen that afternoon. Two days later, his body was found on the island. The circumstances of his death have fueled public suspicion. Wells, who was African American, had been partying with a mostly white friend group – a detail that gained traction online as some referenced Mississippi’s past with racial violence. In late September, a Mississippi grand jury declined to file criminal charges, finding Wells’s death to appear “consistent with drowning”. Jackson county district attorney Angel Myers McIlrath has said Wells’s death was not racially motivated. Wells’s parents and civil rights lawyer Ben Crump continue to call for further investigations, citing the state’s autopsy report, which said Wells’s airways and stomach were empty. His family has said the lack of water found undermines the drowning determination. “I cannot take that ruling, and I cannot move on with my life,” Christine Wonsley, Wells’s mother, reportedly said , referring to the grand jury’s findings at a Monday press conference. “We have been left with more questions and heartbreak than any answers.” Explore more on these topics Mississippi news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed US news US politics Midterms 2026 World Climate crisis Middle East Ukraine US immigration Soccer Business Environment Tech Science Newsletters The Filter Wellness
